---
title: "Rendering"
---

## Specifications

`toArray()` returns the Vega-Lite specification and `toJson()` encodes it. Plots also implement `JsonSerializable`. The specification declares the Vega-Lite 6 schema.

Four escape hatches reach the parts of Vega-Lite that phit does not wrap:

- `raw([...])` deep-merges arbitrary Vega-Lite into the top level. Nested objects merge, and lists and scalars replace.
- `transform(...)` adds Vega-Lite transforms that run before every layer.
- `layer([...])` adds a raw Vega-Lite layer.
- `param()` and `select()` add raw parameters.

## HTML

`embed()` returns a container element followed by the script tags, and `html()` returns a standalone page. Both pass vega-embed options, such as `['actions' => false]` or `['renderer' => 'svg']`.

The container carries the specification in a `data-phit` attribute. A small loader script, about 100 lines, renders every such element with vega-embed. It renders them again when the attribute changes. The same markup therefore works in static pages, Blade views, and Livewire components.

The browser libraries are pinned:

| Library | Version |
| --- | --- |
| vega | 6.4.0 |
| vega-lite | 6.4.3 |
| vega-embed | 7.3.0 |

`Assets` chooses where they come from:

```php
use Phit\Assets;

$plot->embed(assets: Assets::cdn());                 // jsDelivr, with subresource integrity (the default)
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::local('/js/vega'));     // copies you serve: vega.min.js, vega-lite.min.js, vega-embed.min.js
$plot->html(assets: Assets::inline('/path/to/js'));  // embedded in the page, for offline files
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::none());                // your bundle already sets window.vegaEmbed
$plot->embed(assets: false);                         // just the container
```

## Static export

`svg()`, `png()`, `pdf()`, and `save()` run the [vl-convert](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert) command-line tool. It renders without a browser, which suits reports, email, and print. vl-convert bundles its own Vega-Lite, and phit runs it with Vega-Lite 6.1. The test suite validates every specification against the Vega-Lite 6.1 schema, so the same specification renders in both places.

```php
$plot->save('figure.svg');
$plot->save('figure.png', scale: 3);
file_put_contents('figure.pdf', $plot->pdf());
```

phit finds the binary through the `PHIT_VL_CONVERT` or `VL_CONVERT` environment variable, then `PATH`. Download it from the [vl-convert releases](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases). Version 1.9.0 is tested. If the binary is missing, phit throws `Phit\Exceptions\VlConvertNotFound` with these instructions. `new Export(binary: ..., timeout: ..., fontDir: ...)` sets the binary path, the timeout, and an extra font directory explicitly.
